title: Flex CEO Revathi Advaithi Pledges $1 Million for Women's Scholarships at BITS Pilani
excerpt: The Indian American business leader and her husband announced a permanent endowment for women students from economically weaker backgrounds during the institute's 2026 convocation.
body:
• Flex CEO Revathi Advaithi and husband Jeevan Mulgund have donated $1 million (approximately ₹8.6 crore) to BITS Pilani to establish a permanent scholarship endowment for women students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.
  • The scholarship, named after their mothers — Visalam Swamy and Sucheta Mulgund — was announced during the BITS Pilani Convocation 2026 on July 19, where 1,477 students graduated.
  • Advaithi, a BITS Pilani Class of 1990 alumna who was the only woman in her mechanical engineering batch, has been CEO of Flex since 2019 and is a perennial presence on Fortune's Most Powerful Women list.
  • The endowment is designed to run in perpetuity, ensuring that financial constraints do not prevent talented women from accessing a BITS Pilani education.

Revathi Advaithi, the Indian-born CEO of global manufacturing giant Flex, and her husband Jeevan Mulgund have committed $1 million to their alma mater, the Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS) Pilani, to create a permanent scholarship fund for women students from economically weaker backgrounds.

The couple announced the endowment during the BITS Pilani Convocation 2026 on July 19, where Advaithi served as chief guest and addressed the graduating class of 1,477 students at the Pilani campus.

A Scholarship Named After Their Mothers

The endowment has been named the Vishalam Swami and Sucheta Mulgund Scholarship, honoring the mothers of both Advaithi and Mulgund. The couple said the decision was deeply personal, rooted in the belief that educating a daughter can transform an entire family.

"We are naming this scholarship after our mothers, Visalam Swamy and Sucheta Mulgund, because everything we have been able to do began with them. We hope that every young woman who receives this scholarship knows that someone believed in her before she ever walked through the gates."

— Revathi Advaithi and Jeevan Mulgund

The scholarship will provide long-term financial support to deserving women students, ensuring that a lack of funds does not prevent them from pursuing higher education at one of India's premier engineering institutions. At approximately ₹8.6 crore, the endowment is structured to run in perpetuity.

From Only Woman in Class to Fortune 500 CEO

Advaithi's personal connection to BITS Pilani runs deep. She graduated in 1990 with a degree in mechanical engineering — the only woman in her batch. Born in Gujarat into a Tamil family, she grew up across Bihar, Assam, and Chennai before attending the institute.

After completing her MBA at the Thunderbird School of Global Management, Advaithi began her career on a factory floor in Shawnee, Oklahoma, as a shop floor supervisor. She went on to hold leadership positions at Honeywell and Eaton before becoming CEO of Flex in February 2019 — at the time, one of only 24 women leading a Fortune 500 company.

Under her leadership, Flex has grown into a $26 billion global manufacturing and supply chain solutions provider with operations in 30 countries. Advaithi has been named to Fortune's Most Powerful Women list every year from 2019 through 2025 and was recognized as Fast Company's Modern CEO of the Year.

BITS Pilani Welcomes the Endowment

BITS Pilani Vice-Chancellor Prof. V. Ramgopal Rao praised the contribution, calling it a model for alumni engagement.

"By endowing scholarships in perpetuity, she is ensuring that generations of talented young women will benefit from her generosity. This strengthens our commitment to admitting the finest students, irrespective of their financial circumstances."

— Prof. V. Ramgopal Rao, Vice-Chancellor, BITS Pilani

Campus Director Sudhirkumar Barai added that an endowed scholarship is "one of the most enduring gifts an alumna can give to her institution, as it continues well beyond a lifetime and quietly transforms one life after another."

The institute has been on an upward trajectory, recently climbing to 7th position in India's NIRF University rankings. BITS Pilani has secured over ₹650 crore in cumulative research funding and has expansion projects worth over ₹1,200 crore underway across its campuses.

Diaspora Philanthropy and What's Next

The donation adds to a growing trend of Indian American leaders directing philanthropy back to Indian educational institutions. Advaithi, who also serves on Uber's board of directors and the MIT Presidential CEO Advisory Board, has long championed women in STEM and manufacturing through mentorship and industry coalitions.

For BITS Pilani, the endowment comes as the institute works to expand its global footprint — it recently launched a dual-degree Bachelor of Computer Science program with Australia's RMIT University. The Vishalam Swami and Sucheta Mulgund Scholarship will begin supporting its first cohort of women students in the upcoming academic year.
